items.title: Russia strikes Dnipro train station in central Ukraine, killing 14
items.brief: A Russian drone struck the main railway station in the central Ukrainian city of Dnipro as people waited to board a train on Thursday morning, killing 14 people.

items.title: Hegseth ousts Pentagon’s chief planner as renewed action against Iran looms, source says
items.brief: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has fired the Pentagon’s top planning officer as President Donald Trump weighs new strikes against Iran, according to a defense official and another source familiar with the matter.

items.title: Last snapshot of the US economy before midterms shows stronger growth but higher inflation
items.brief: US economic growth accelerated last quarter at its fastest pace in a year; however, rising gas prices helped to lift inflation in September to a four-month high, new data showed Thursday.

items.title: Is Fox News pivoting to its post-Trump era? The answer lies in what it is — and isn’t — showing
items.brief: President Donald Trump is “dominating the airwaves and controlling the conversation,” Fox News host Jesse Watters declared on October 21, touting the president’s midterm campaign blitz.

items.title: DoorDash is buying Instacart for $17 billion
items.brief: DoorDash is buying rival Instacart in a deal worth roughly $17 billion, signaling that the delivery wars continue to heat up.

items.title: What caused the deadly train crash in Spain? What we know so far
items.brief: Spain has begun three days of national mourning after 69 people were killed and over 100 injured in a high-speed train collision, the third deadly incident this year on the country’s rail network.

items.title: Manhunt for escaped Tennessee murder convict crosses state lines after the truck he stole is found abandoned in Illinois
items.brief: The search for a convicted murderer who escaped from a Tennessee prison has crossed state lines after authorities found his stolen getaway truck in southern Illinois.

items.title: Final Israeli election results are almost in. Netanyahu hasn’t won – but he hasn’t lost either
items.brief: In a political career that has spanned more than three decades, Benjamin Netanyahu has been written off too many times to count, only to prove the obituaries were penned prematurely.
